source.title: Generalization Ability of Wide Residual Networks
source.authors: Jian-Fa Lai; Zixiong Yu; Song-Tao Tian; Qian Lin

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies residual networks under varying label corruption and reports effects on training-time landmarks and test accuracy, using a different setup from the original random-label experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports synthetic-data results for squared and cross-entropy losses and CIFAR-10 results in Figures 1–2. The captions explicitly describe increasing time gaps as corruption rises. Test-accuracy values are figure-only; no precise values or textual trend are provided. The study does not report fully random labels.
record.test_reason: The corruption experiments examine near-zero training-label error and training-time landmarks in residual networks. They bear on fitting partially corrupted labels, but the reported timing gap does not establish V2's convergence-speed claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's experimental paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors also prove uniform approximation by RNTK regression, minimax generalization with suitable early stopping, and poor generalization rates after loss interpolation. Their experiments argue that signal strength determines whether near-zero classification error occurs close to optimal stopping.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies label corruption and analyzes stopping-time and test-accuracy behavior in residual networks; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The time gap is reported to increase with corruption ratio. Synthetic experiments use two losses; the CIFAR-10 experiment uses cross-entropy.

fits_no_version.finding: The gap between optimal test stopping and near-zero training-label error grows with corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing label corruption separates optimal generalization time from the time of near-zero training classification error.

fits_no_version.finding: Wide residual networks under the stated noisy-regression assumptions achieve minimax rates with early stopping and have slow excess-risk decay when trained to interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early stopping improves generalization rates for sufficiently wide residual networks in this regression setting.

record.problems: The cited experimental outcome is primarily in figures. The text gives no precise plotted values, and experiments stop at corruption p = 0.6. The theoretical results concern regression and do not directly test random-label image classification.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 test-accuracy curves and Figure 2 test accuracy are not extracted as separate rows: their values and trends are only in figures, with no textual description sufficient to determine the result against V4. No other result bearing on the claim is reported.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, chance test performance at full corruption, and fitting without architecture or hyperparameter changes.
Small constant-factor training cost and absolute time to convergence as corruption increases; the supplied text reports only differences between stopping landmarks.

Full corruption, exact perfect training fit, and a readable test-error trend steadily approaching chance. Synthetic test labels are themselves corrupted, complicating interpretation as retention of clean signal.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their removal.
Separate learning trajectories for real patterns and noisy labels. Optimal test stopping before near-zero training error does not directly measure their learning order.

missing.what: Record the near-zero training-label-error landmark separately from its gap relative to optimal stopping, including the attained error or threshold if available. This is the fitting component relevant to V4.
missing.locator: Section 5; Figures 1–2 and the definition of tlabel

record.verdict_notes: The record's V2 limits_scope verdict is unwarranted: an unmeasured training-time ratio is an untested component, not a demonstrated limitation. Test-accuracy curves were explicitly declared in rows_left_out and are unreadable in the supplied text, so no additional missing entry or verdict is assigned to their trends.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test completely random labels or report training and test error for that condition.
No small-constant-factor comparison of total training time is reported; corruption is tested only through 0.6.
No shuffled-pixel or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.
Corruption is tested only through 0.6, not all labels; the text does not establish perfect training fit at each corruption level or a textual trend in test error.
Weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation are not tested.
The study does not test whether real patterns are learned before noisy labels.

rows.subject: residual fully-connected network
rows.operation_detail: Trained on synthetic data with labels corrupted at varying rates; measured the gap between tlabel and topt.
rows.measure: time gap between tlabel and topt
rows.value: Figure only; caption says the gap increases as p increases.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars show the mean and standard deviation over 10 replicate experiments.
rows.note: The caption describes the trend; the figure contains the plotted values.
rows.check: The reported increase concerns tlabel minus topt, not total time to fit labels. Without the individual stopping times, this cannot establish slower convergence or a small constant-factor cost. Synthetic test labels are also corrupted.

rows.measure: time gap between tlabel and topt
rows.value: Figure only; caption says the gap increases as p increases.

rows.subject: convolutional residual network
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with label corruption; measured the gap between tlabel and topt.
rows.measure: time gap between tlabel and topt
rows.value: Figure only; caption says the gap increases as p increases.
rows.note: The caption describes the trend; the figure contains the plotted values.
rows.check: The caption establishes a growing gap relative to optimal stopping, not increasing absolute convergence time. No constant-factor comparison is available. Section 5 inconsistently calls the trained model Alex after describing a convolutional residual network; the architecture supports the row's subject.

relationships.condition: Near-zero training-label error component only, for the reported corruption sweep p = 0 through 0.6
relationships.reason: Section 5 and Figures 1–2 report timing landmarks defined by near-zero training-label error across the corruption sweep, supporting approximate fitting of partially corrupted labels. This rests on the text and the missing fitting-result rows, not on the gap values in R1–R3.
relationships.display_finding: Training-label error approached zero across the corruption sweep from p = 0 through 0.6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
